Usage: drive wait <session> [flags]

Block until a session's turn ends, then print how it ended.

The wait ends when the turn has stayed over for --quiet, or the session
stops on a prompt; at once on an API error or an interrupt. It prints the
end of the reply, the view to act on, and next: where the ending decides
what to do. A driver that waits itself runs it in the background; a chat
driver is woken instead (drive watch).

Arguments:
  <session>              The session to wait for.

Flags:
      --quiet=SECONDS    How long the turn must stay over before the wait ends, so a session that
                         pauses between tools is not taken for done (default: 60).
      --bg=SECONDS       How long to wait on a turn that ended while background jobs it started
                         still run; such a turn usually resumes when they finish (default: 600).
      --json             Print one JSON document instead of text.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help             Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME       Act in this batch instead of the current one, which stays current. It may
                         stand anywhere on the line.

JSON:
  session, block, state, error (kind, text, at: the API error that ended the turn), shells
  (jobs this turn started, still running), orphans (older jobs), jobs (started, command),
  reply (its end), screen (its end, for a prompt the transcript does not show), view, next

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
